spatial_claims.claim: D lies on segment AG between A and G, since AD is the second apotome with annex DG, and AG = AD + DG
E is the midpoint of segment DG
H lies on segment AG such that rect(AH, HG) = sq(EG), positioned between A and G by the application of areas construction
AH and HG are commensurable in length (by 10.17, since sq(AG) > sq(DG) by a square commensurable with AG)
Semicircle described on AG as diameter; K lies on the semicircle above line AG
HK is perpendicular to AG at H, meeting the semicircle at K
Angle AKG is right, being an angle in a semicircle (by 3.31)
KH is the altitude of right triangle AKG to hypotenuse AG
sq(AK) = AH * AG (projection formula from right triangle with altitude, by 6.8)
sq(GK) = HG * AG (projection formula from right triangle with altitude, by 6.8)
sq(AK) + sq(GK) = sq(AG) by Pythagorean theorem (1.47), since angle AKG is right
KH = EG, since sq(KH) = rect(AH, HG) = sq(EG)

configuration_map: Points on line AG (left to right): A --- H --- D --- E --- G. D lies between A and G (AD is second apotome, DG is annex). E is midpoint of DG. H is between A and G positioned by application of areas so that rect(AH, HG) = sq(EG), with AH commensurable to HG. Point K is above line AG on the semicircle with diameter AG, with HK perpendicular to AG. Triangle AKG has a right angle at K (angle in semicircle). Lines MN and NO (Steps 10-16) are abstract algebraic constructs defined by sq(MN) + sq(NO) = rect(AC, AG) and rect(MN, NO) = (1/2) rect(AC, DG), with no spatial position in the figure.
pass_reason: All spatial claims in the geometric construction (semicircle on AG, perpendicular HK, right triangle AKG, altitude relations) are mutually consistent and follow standard Euclidean constructions. The projection formulas, Pythagorean theorem application, and length equality KH = EG are all compatible with the established configuration. The bulk of the proof (Steps 9-16) is algebraic manipulation of commensurability and area relationships involving abstract lines MN and NO, which make no spatial claims that could conflict with the geometry. No angle decomposition errors or point position contradictions were found.
